subject.title: fix(active-memory): bound legacy toggle migration reads

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the 8 MiB hard stop that leaves oversized legacy Active Memory opt-out files in place and unmigrated, or require a different bounded recovery path before merging?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically coherent, but choosing whether existing persisted opt-outs may be skipped on upgrade is a product and compatibility policy decision rather than a purely local code correction.

options.title: Accept bounded skip policy
options.body: Merge the PR and treat the visible warning plus retained source file as the supported recovery path for unusually large legacy state.

options.title: Require alternate recovery
options.body: Keep the bounded reader but define and prove a memory-safe migration or repair path that preserves oversized users’ opt-outs.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded skip policy
recommendation.body: Merge the PR and treat the visible warning plus retained source file as the supported recovery path for unusually large legacy state.
